svg.text: Local safety: Node 1 guards the fan when the broker is gone
Concept 10 · Node 1 firmware v1.5.0 · numbers from the author's Wokwi test: temp_fan_on 31 °C, broker cut with test offline
Pi's LAN cable unplugged, broker off,
or the Serial command test offline
cable is noticed only 15–30 seconds later
OFFLINE MODE on the status page
rule turns the fan on by itself
so the backend has time to subscribe
whoever turned it on turns it off:
Thresholds from the server, stored in NVS
The server publishes config retained (QoS 1) whenever a fan rule changes:
Node 1 checks it (a number 15–45 °C), then saves temp_fan_on in NVS:
the number survives a power cut.
As long as it has never received config: default 30 °C.
The fan turns off again below temp_fan_on − 2 (a fixed 2 °C gap).
A gap you should know about
Local safety only works when the broker is unreachable.
If what goes down is the backend on the laptop, while the broker on the Pi
keeps running, Node 1 stays connected and never enters
offline mode, even though the server rules stop too.
The fix: a backend on a server that's always on (Modules 26–27).
